title: The role of polarization field terms in a model for a cavity quantum material
summary: Constructing models for cavity quantum materials requires a careful treatment of the light-matter coupling. In general, one must specify matrix elements constructed from the material wavefunctions, which are often unknown in a tight-binding framework. The Peierls substitution is frequently used to avoid introducing these additional parameters in the multi-center dipole (or Peierls) gauge, under the assumption that contributions from intraband and interband dipole moments can be neglected.
